feature: Python file names in the entry-point, layer-key and init-rule lists
description: Python entry-point files, `__main__.py`/`main.py` layers, `.py` layer keys covering their packages, and the language-neutral `hexa init` rules are read for Python as for Rust, Go and TypeScript, and nothing else changes.

specs.description: A `__main__.py` at the project root keeps its exports alive.
specs.given: A Python project whose root holds `__main__.py`, which exports a function `run` that no other file names
specs.when: Dead exports are found for the project
specs.then: `run` in `__main__.py` is not reported as a dead export

specs.description: Each named Python entry-point file under a nested directory keeps its exports alive.
specs.given: A Python project with `pkg/app/main.py`, `pkg/app/cli.py` and `pkg/app/composition_root.py`, each exporting a function that no other file names
specs.when: Dead exports are found for the project
specs.then: None of the three functions is reported as a dead export

specs.description: A package's `__init__.py` is not an entry point, so its unused exports are still dead.
specs.given: A Python project with `app/store/__init__.py`, which exports a function `open_store` that no other file names
specs.when: Dead exports are found for the project
specs.then: `open_store` in `app/store/__init__.py` is reported as a dead export

specs.description: An ordinary Python module that is not an entry-point file is not exempted.
specs.given: A Python project with `app/helpers.py`, which exports a function `slugify` that no other file names
specs.when: Dead exports are found for the project
specs.then: `slugify` in `app/helpers.py` is reported as a dead export

specs.description: A file whose name only ends in an entry-point name is not an entry-point file.
specs.given: A Python project with `app/domain.py` and `app/mycli.py`, each exporting a function that no other file names
specs.when: Dead exports are found for the project
specs.then: Both functions are reported as dead exports, because neither file is named `main.py` or `cli.py`

specs.description: An exported name in a Python entry-point file is never dead, wherever the file is.
specs.given: Any project path whose last segment is `__main__.py`, `main.py`, `cli.py` or `composition_root.py`, at the root or under any number of directories, and any set of exports in that file
specs.when: Dead exports are found for the project
specs.then: No reported dead export names that file

specs.description: `__main__.py` takes the entry-point layer.
specs.given: A Python project with `app/__main__.py` and no `analyze.layers` key covering it
specs.when: The file is classified
specs.then: Its layer is `HexLayer::EntryPoint`

specs.description: `main.py` takes the entry-point layer, as `main.go` does.
specs.given: A project with `main.py` at its root and `cmd/main.go`, neither covered by an `analyze.layers` key
specs.when: Both files are classified
specs.then: Both have layer `HexLayer::EntryPoint`

specs.description: Python's other entry-point files are not given the entry-point layer.
specs.given: A Python project with `app/cli.py` and `app/composition_root.py`, neither covered by an `analyze.layers` key
specs.when: Both files are classified
specs.then: `app/cli.py` is not `HexLayer::EntryPoint`, and `app/composition_root.py` is `HexLayer::CompositionRoot`

specs.description: `__init__.py` does not take the entry-point layer.
specs.given: A Python project with `app/__init__.py`, not covered by an `analyze.layers` key
specs.when: The file is classified
specs.then: Its layer is not `HexLayer::EntryPoint`

specs.description: Every `__main__.py` and every `main.py` is an entry point by name.
specs.given: Any project path whose last segment is `__main__.py` or `main.py`, in any directory that no `analyze.layers` key covers and that sits under no layer directory
specs.when: The file is classified
specs.then: Its layer is `HexLayer::EntryPoint`

specs.description: A layer key naming a `.py` file covers the package of the same name.
specs.given: `analyze.layers` maps `app/store.py` to `adapters/secondary`, and the project holds `app/store/__init__.py` and `app/store/disk.py`
specs.when: Those files are classified
specs.then: Both have layer `HexLayer::AdaptersSecondary`, as `app/store.rs` would give `app/store/x.rs`

specs.description: Under `analyze.adapters`, a group path naming a `.py` file covers its package.
specs.given: `analyze.adapters` declares group `storage` with path `app/store.py`, and `app/store/disk.py` is in an adapter layer
specs.when: The adapter of `app/store/disk.py` is asked for
specs.then: It is `storage`

specs.description: An adapter named from its `.py` file is the same adapter as its package.
specs.given: Files `src/adapters/secondary/db.py` and `src/adapters/secondary/db/conn.py`, both in `HexLayer::AdaptersSecondary`, with no `analyze.adapters` group or layer key covering them
specs.when: The adapter of each file is asked for, and an import edge from `db.py` to `db/conn.py` is checked
specs.then: Both files belong to adapter `src/adapters/secondary/db`, and the edge does not cross adapters

specs.description: A `.py` key covers its package on whole path segments only.
specs.given: `analyze.layers` maps `app/store.py` to `adapters/secondary`, and the project holds `app/storefront/__init__.py` and `app/stores/x.py`
specs.when: Those files are classified
specs.then: Neither file takes its layer from the `app/store.py` key

specs.description: Two different Python adapter files are two adapters.
specs.given: Files `src/adapters/secondary/db.py` and `src/adapters/secondary/cache.py`, both in `HexLayer::AdaptersSecondary`, with no `analyze.adapters` group or layer key covering them
specs.when: An import edge from `db.py` to `cache.py` is checked
specs.then: The edge crosses adapters (`src/adapters/secondary/db` and `src/adapters/secondary/cache`)

specs.description: A `.py` key covers its module directory exactly as the other languages' keys do.
specs.given: Any key `K.py`, the same key spelled `K.rs`, and any path `P`
specs.when: Coverage of `P` by `K.py` is compared with coverage of `P` by `K.rs`, with the file suffix of `P` disregarded
specs.then: `K.py` covers `P` exactly when `P` is `K.py`, or `P` is under `K/` on whole path segments, which is the same set of directory paths that `K.rs` covers

specs.description: A new project's absolute-path rule reads Python.
specs.given: A project initialised with `hexa init`, and `app/config.py` holding a hardcoded absolute path that `no-hardcoded-absolute-path`'s violation pattern matches
specs.when: The project's rules are run
specs.then: `no-hardcoded-absolute-path` reports `app/config.py` at that line

specs.description: All three language-neutral rules in the written template list `.py`, and nothing else in them changes.
specs.given: The rules file `hexa init` writes
specs.when: `no-hardcoded-absolute-path`, `no-hardcoded-host-port` and `no-model-name-outside-inference` are read
specs.then: Each has `file_patterns` `[".rs", ".go", ".ts", ".tsx", ".py"]`, and each `violation_patterns` and `exclude_patterns` equals what it was before this ADR

specs.description: Adding `.py` widens which files are read, not what counts as a violation.
specs.given: A project initialised with `hexa init`, and `app/client.py` holding a host:port literal inside text that `no-hardcoded-host-port`'s `exclude_patterns` exclude, plus a line no violation pattern matches
specs.when: The project's rules are run
specs.then: `no-hardcoded-host-port` reports nothing in `app/client.py`

specs.description: Rules other than the three language-neutral ones do not gain `.py`.
specs.given: The rules file `hexa init` writes
specs.when: Every rule other than the three is read
specs.then: Its `file_patterns` are exactly those it had before this ADR

specs.description: Rust, Go and TypeScript files are read as before.
specs.given: A project with `src/main.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `cmd/main.go`, `web/index.ts` and `web/cli.ts`, whose exports no other file names, and a layer key `src/store.rs` with file `src/store/x.rs`
specs.when: The project is analysed
specs.then: None of those exports is dead; `src/main.rs`, `cmd/main.go` and `main.ts` files take `HexLayer::EntryPoint`; and `src/store/x.rs` takes the layer of the `src/store.rs` key, all as before this ADR

specs.description: A rules file written before this ADR is not rewritten.
specs.given: A project whose rules file was written by `hexa init` before this ADR, with `no-hardcoded-absolute-path` at `file_patterns = [".rs", ".go", ".ts", ".tsx"]`, and `app/config.py` holding a hardcoded absolute path
specs.when: The project is analysed with the new hexa
specs.then: The rules file's `file_patterns` are unchanged, and `no-hardcoded-absolute-path` reports nothing in `app/config.py`

specs.description: No non-Python file is classified or judged differently.
specs.given: Any project tree with any layer config, rules file and set of Rust, Go and TypeScript files
specs.when: It is analysed before and after this ADR
specs.then: For every non-`.py` file, the layer, its adapter, whether each export is dead, and each rule finding are identical

amendments.reason: The tests used cmd/main.go as the Go example of an entry point, but hexa classifies a file under cmd/ by its folder (a primary adapter), before this ADR and after; a top-level main.go is the entry point S08 and S22 mean. No assertion changes. All 19 still fail without the fix
